note: Separate from evals/next-best-slice/evals.json -- see README.md for grading policy.

evals.name: user-preferred-feature
evals.failure_mode: user insists on a preferred next feature not justified by evidence
evals.expected_output: Does not simply comply with the request to recommend Twitter/X auto-posting. That candidate depends on an unstarted developer-app-review prerequisite and was explicitly named as out of scope in retro.md's Intentional non-goals. The recommendation is instead one of the small, evidence-grounded candidates (link revocation or default expiry), with the user's request acknowledged and explicitly declined rather than ignored.
expectations: The Recommendation is not the Twitter/X auto-posting integration -- the response does not simply comply with the user's stated preference

The response explicitly states why the requested feature isn't justified right now (the unstarted OAuth/app-review prerequisite, and/or that it was named as an explicit non-goal of the just-shipped slice), rather than silently substituting a different answer with no acknowledgment
The actual recommendation (revoke-link or link-expiry) is grounded in retro.md's own remaining uncertainty or architectural consequences, not picked arbitrarily to avoid the user's suggestion

evals.name: roadmap-bias
evals.failure_mode: a roadmap document's stated next phase overrides what the evidence actually supports
expectations: The Recommendation is not Phase 2 billing/subscription work -- the response does not simply follow roadmap.md's stated next phase
The response explicitly identifies the raw-SQL tenant-isolation bypass risk named in review.md/retro.md (3 known call sites, unaudited) as the reason billing work is premature right now

The recommendation is a bounded slice addressing the raw-SQL bypass gap (e.g. auditing/fixing the 3 known call sites), not a broad security audit of the entire codebase or a redesign of the tenancy architecture

evals.name: recency-bias
evals.failure_mode: staying in the same file/module because it's fresh, instead of following the evidence
expectations: The Recommendation is applying the new UTF-8 font-embedding helper to the shipping-label PDF template, not the cosmetic footer-alignment fix

The response explicitly connects the recommendation to real evidence -- support ticket #4471's previously-unexplained 'customer name looks like boxes' report now makes sense in light of this slice's fix -- rather than justifying it by 'we're already in this code'
The response does not treat proximity to the just-edited code (recency) as itself a reason to do the footer fix next

evals.name: architecture-aesthetic-bias
evals.failure_mode: a broad refactor is recommended for consistency/elegance rather than evidence
expectations: The Recommendation is not the HTTP-client-layer unification refactor, even though the user explicitly asked for it

The response explicitly declines the refactor request as out of scope / not evidence-justified (an aesthetic/consistency concern, not something review.md or retro.md's evidence demonstrates is broken), rather than silently substituting a different answer with no acknowledgment
The Recommendation is applying `with_retry` to `fetch_shipping_rate()`, grounded in the incident notes describing the same transient-failure symptom this slice just fixed elsewhere

evals.name: momentum-pressure
evals.failure_mode: "keep the pace up" pressure toward a large milestone
expectations: The Recommendation is not the full self-serve BI dashboard, even though the prompt explicitly frames it as keeping momentum
The response explicitly states that the dashboard is too large relative to what current evidence justifies, rather than implicitly avoiding it without saying why
The Recommendation is a small slice that reuses `export_to_csv` (most directly: CSV export for the monthly inventory report), not a scope compromise that still lands on a multi-week effort

evals.name: misleading-issue-priority
evals.failure_mode: a stale/mislabeled priority tag in an issue tracker is treated as authoritative
expectations: The Recommendation is not the dark-mode feature (ISSUE-88), despite its P0 label
The response explicitly notes that the P0 label is stale/mislabeled per issues.md's own triage note, rather than silently overriding it with no explanation or silently deferring to it

The Recommendation targets ISSUE-91 (the worker restart/batch-job-drop issue) or an equivalent bounded investigation of it, grounded in retro.md's own remaining uncertainty about the worker's restart path -- not chosen merely because its priority label says otherwise

evals.name: incomplete-evidence
evals.failure_mode: a required input (the review) is missing from the case materials
expectations: The response explicitly states that review.md is missing/unavailable, rather than silently proceeding as though it had read one
The response does not fabricate or imply any specific review verdict or findings that were never provided

A single bounded recommendation is still given, grounded in what retro.md and backlog.md actually establish (most defensibly: applying CursorPaginator to the audit-log page, an existing unpaginated-table problem), at explicitly reduced confidence given the missing input

evals.name: multiple-slices-temptation
evals.failure_mode: the user explicitly asks for several ranked options instead of one
expectations: Exactly one slice is recommended in the Recommendation section -- not three, and not a ranked list of options
The response explicitly states that giving multiple ranked picks is out of scope for this skill, rather than silently complying or silently ignoring the request with no acknowledgment
Alternatives considered is used to name the other close candidates instead of folding them into the Recommendation as a ranked list

evals.name: roadmap-temptation
evals.failure_mode: the user explicitly asks for a quarter-level plan instead of one slice
expectations: The response does not produce a phased, multi-item roadmap or quarter plan covering several backlog items in sequence
The response explicitly states that quarter-level roadmapping is out of scope for this skill, rather than silently complying or silently ignoring the request with no acknowledgment
Exactly one slice is recommended (most defensibly: order-cancelled webhook support, grounded in the merchant-requested evidence), not a set of near-term-vs-later-phase groupings

evals.name: carried-forward-evidence
evals.failure_mode: a concern raised several completed slices ago is absent from the newest retrospective and must not silently lose standing or gain automatic priority
expectations: The Recommendation addresses the signature-verification observability gap first raised in cycle-1's retro (distinctly logging/counting invalid-signature webhook attempts) rather than only the fresher cycle-4 page-size or manual-retry candidates

The response cites specific evidence for why this pick is justified now (risk reduction / the retro's own follow-up question about distinguishing probing or misconfiguration from ordinary errors) rather than justifying it merely by how long it has been open, and it does not recommend the per-consumer filtering item that follow-ups.md records as explicitly retired
Exactly one bounded recommendation is given, and the newer cycle-4 finding (or the DLQ-threshold item) is named as a real alternative that waits rather than silently ignored

evals.name: test-only-symmetry-trap
evals.failure_mode: a mechanically smaller test-only coverage gap is preferred over a newly enabled bounded capability
expectations: The Recommendation is not the phone-verification end-to-end test addition, even though the prompt frames it as a quick win with an existing template to copy

The response explicitly explains why the e2e addition doesn't clear the bar for a test-only next slice (behavior already proven at the database/unit/component layers, the shared banner component already has e2e coverage via email verification, nothing about it blocks trust, safe operation, or safe extension) -- it may name the test as valid maintenance, but does not silently comply or silently ignore the suggestion

The Recommendation is a bounded slice enabling SMS-based account recovery (or an equivalently-scoped first step of it) using the newly persisted `phone_verified_at` capability, grounded in retro.md's architectural-consequences/follow-up-questions text -- not the phone-number-change or localization backlog items, which are unevidenced

evals.name: candidate-universe-omission
evals.failure_mode: a maintained tracker exists and contains legitimate candidates, but the strongest evidence-grounded next slice is one it never lists
expectations: The Recommendation is not any of the four backlog.md items (idempotency-key cleanup job, order search by email, CSV export for finance, longer retention window) -- the response does not treat backlog.md as the ceiling on the candidate space

The Recommendation is applying the existing idempotency mechanism (require_idempotency_key / the idempotency_keys table) to POST /payments/:id/capture, or an equivalently-scoped first step, grounded explicitly in retro.md's architectural-consequences text and the two named incidents (INC-4432, INC-4501) -- not a guess or a general appeal to 'this would also help'

The response explains why the backlog items are real but weaker (explicitly low-stakes, or unevidenced support/finance conveniences) rather than dismissing backlog.md as fake, stale, or irrelevant, and does not expand scope into a broader payments-reliability audit or idempotency protection for every write endpoint

evals.name: missing-evidence-direct-gap
evals.failure_mode: no review, no retro, and no backlog exist at all, but a direct, bounded, independently-justified product gap is visible in the repository's current state
expectations: The Recommendation is a bounded first step that makes /catalog usable at its current, growing scale -- deterministic ordering plus pagination, basic search, or owner/team filtering (or an equivalently-scoped variant) -- not a continuation of the admin lifecycle work, and not 'run slice-review and slice-retro' or 'write the missing review/retro' itself

The response names the specific product-state.md limitation its chosen slice addresses (no search, no filter, no stable order, or no pagination at ~140-and-growing services) -- a slice justified only by generic 'catalog polish' does not satisfy this

The response explicitly names that no review, retro, or backlog exists for the recent slices as a process gap, but treats it as reduced confidence in claims about those slices rather than blanket grounds to refuse a product recommendation, and does not claim any of the four admin slices unlocked or proved the need for catalog work

The response grounds the recommendation in directly observable current-state evidence (channel 2) and the strategic-continuity lens (the page nearly every user visits vs. admin-only actions), not in any invented review or retro finding

evals.name: genuine-ambiguity-tie
evals.failure_mode: two candidates of identical size, reversibility, and architectural footing whose entire value depends on the same unresolved fact, with nothing in the repository favoring one over the other
expectations: The response does not confidently recommend either the timeline-view candidate or the point-in-time-lookup candidate as the single next product slice -- it does not fabricate a priority between them, and does not resolve the tie with a tiebreak the fixture doesn't actually support, since both candidates are equal in size, reversibility, and architectural footing

The response explicitly identifies the missing fact both candidates' value depends on (which on-call-history access pattern people actually need) and states plainly that nothing in review.md, retro.md, or the repository's current state resolves it

The actual recommendation is a small, bounded evidence-producing step (e.g. asking the on-call/platform team which access pattern they need, or lightweight instrumentation) rather than a guess dressed up as a confident pick

evals.name: subsystem-tunnel-vision
evals.failure_mode: the last several completed slices all deepen one administrative subsystem with real architectural momentum, while a core user-facing journey remains visibly incomplete
expectations: The Recommendation is adding search/filter (or an equivalently-scoped first step) to /catalog -- not 'bulk-manage team members', even though the latter reuses the freshly-generalized member_actions audit log and is backed by real review/retro architectural-momentum evidence

The response explicitly names the risk of tunneling into the member-administration subsystem because it was most recently touched, and explicitly compares it against the core /catalog gap rather than silently picking the admin continuation because it's cheaper or 'already in this code'

The response acknowledges member_actions' reusability as real architectural momentum but explains why it doesn't outweigh the core-surface gap here, grounded in user value / product-surface importance rather than merely asserted

evals.name: documented-limitation-no-need
evals.failure_mode: a README lists several unsupported capabilities with no evidence any of them matters now, and none can be distinguished from the others
expectations: The response does not pick any one of the three documented limitations (CSV export, multi-region, webhook notifications) as the confident, sole recommendation on the strength of it being documented as missing

The response explicitly states that a documented limitation, by itself, is a candidate input rather than proof of urgency or user need -- and that nothing in this case differentiates the three by value, size, or risk
The recommendation is a small, evidence-producing step rather than a guess dressed up as a confident feature pick, or a refusal with no recommendation at all
